qa.title: What you need to know before your stay in Sousse.

qaList.q: Do veneers hurt?
qaList.a: No, placing veneers is generally painless or causes little discomfort. Tooth preparation is minimal and, if necessary, local anesthesia can be used to ensure your comfort.

qaList.q: How many sessions are needed?
qaList.a: Generally, 2 to 3 sessions are sufficient:

qaList.q: Is the shade natural?
qaList.a: Yes. The shade is chosen based on your face, your skin tone and your natural teeth to achieve a harmonious and realistic result.

qaList.q: How long do ceramic veneers last?
qaList.a: With good oral hygiene and regular follow-up, ceramic veneers can last between 10 and 15 years, or even longer.

qaList.q: Can whitening and veneers be combined during the same stay?
qaList.a: Yes. Whitening is often performed before placing veneers to achieve a brighter and perfectly harmonized overall shade.

qaList.q: Is the result visible immediately?
qaList.a: Yes. As soon as the veneers are placed, the change is visible and the smile is transformed instantly.

qaList.q: How to maintain veneers?
qaList.a: Maintenance is simple:
list: Brush your teeth twice a day
Use dental floss or interdental brushes
Have regular check-ups with your dentist
Avoid biting very hard objects (ice cubes, pens, etc.)
qaList.footer: Veneers do not require special care, just good daily oral hygiene.

technologie-de-charge.description: A basal (or cortico-basal) implant can be placed on the same day a tooth is removed, during the same appointment. It anchors in the cortical bone, the densest and deepest part of the jaw. This is what makes it suitable for the large majority of patients, including those with significant bone loss, and often without a bone graft. Here you’ll find how this technique works in Sousse, Tunisia, who it is for, how treatment is organised and what you can expect.

inovation.title: Understanding the basal implant
inovation.answerOneP1: A conventional dental implant relies mainly on the volume of bone around it. When that bone has shrunk, a bone graft and several months of waiting are often needed.
inovation.answerOneP2: A basal implant is thinner. It passes through the weakened area to anchor in the cortical bone, a dense layer that usually remains even when a lot of bone has been lost. In most cases, this anchorage makes it possible to:
list: place the implant in the same session as the extraction;
fit temporary fixed teeth within the following days.
inovation.answerTwo: It requires precise planning, a 3D radiological assessment (cone beam), and advanced surgical mastery. Not all cases are eligible; Dr. Yassine KALLALI evaluates each situation individually.

protocole.title: How does treatment work?

list.title: Extraction and implant placement
list.description: The teeth to be removed are extracted as gently as possible. The basal implants are placed in the same session, under local anaesthesia.

list.title: Fixed teeth
list.description: A fixed tooth or bridge is fitted within the days following surgery. There is no removable denture to wear. The timeline for your final prosthesis is explained at the consultation, according to your treatment plan.

list.title: Follow-up, at the clinic and then remotely
list.description: Check-ups at the clinic before you leave, then video-call follow-up for patients who travelled from abroad. Regular check-ups and good oral hygiene are essential for your treatment to last.

qa.title: What to know before your stay in Sousse.

qaList.q: Can I have a basal implant if I’ve been told I don’t have enough bone?
qaList.a: In the large majority of cases, yes. The basal implant anchors in the cortical bone, which usually remains even after significant bone loss. The 3D scan confirms it.

qaList.q: Can a single tooth be replaced?
qaList.a: Yes. A basal implant can replace a single tooth as well as several teeth or a full arch.

qaList.q: How long is the recovery?
qaList.a: Swelling and discomfort are common for a few days. A soft diet is recommended at first. Dr Kallali gives you written instructions and tells you when you can resume your activities.

qaList.q: Can I fly after the procedure?
qaList.a: Generally yes, once your post-operative check-up has been done at the clinic. Dr Kallali tells you the right return date for your case.

qaList.q: Is follow-up possible from France, Italy or the United Kingdom?
qaList.a: Yes. Video-call follow-up is arranged after you return home. Some check-ups may require a visit to the clinic.

qaList.q: How do I send my X-rays?
qaList.a: You can attach a recent panoramic X-ray or cone beam scan to the form, or send it by WhatsApp or email. If you don’t have one, the assessment will be done at the clinic.

qaList.q: Does it hurt?
qaList.a: The procedure is carried out under local anaesthesia. Some discomfort and swelling are usual in the following days. Pain relief medication is prescribed.

qaList.q: How long does a basal implant last?
qaList.a: It depends on your oral hygiene, regular check-ups, general health and habits such as smoking or teeth grinding. The treatment is designed for long-term use, with regular maintenance.

qaList.q: Which airports serve Sousse?
qaList.a: Three airports serve Sousse: Monastir, about 20 minutes away; Enfidha-Hammamet, about 40 minutes away; Tunis-Carthage, about 1.5 to 2 hours by road. Depending on the season and the airline, direct flights connect these airports with several European cities, including Paris, Milan, Brussels and London. We recommend checking routes when you book.

qaList.q: What accommodation is available in Sousse?
qaList.a: Sousse and the Port El Kantaoui area offer a wide choice of hotels and apartments. The clinic can advise you on accommodation suited to your stay and your recovery.

qaList.q: Recovery time after the procedure?
qaList.a: The length of stay varies according to your clinical situation. For an basal implant, most patients stay between 2 and 5 days to complete the treatment and necessary check-ups.

qaList.q: Can you fly after implant placement?
qaList.a: Yes. In most cases, it is possible to travel by plane 24 to 48 hours after the procedure, provided you follow the post-operative recommendations.

qaList.q: How can I send my X-rays?
qaList.a: You can send your panoramic X-rays, scanners or Cone Beam directly via our secure form, by email or via WhatsApp.

qaList.q: Is it painful?
qaList.a: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia. Most patients describe mild to moderate discomfort during the first few days, generally well controlled by prescribed medications.

qaList.q: What is the lifespan of an basal implant?
qaList.a: With good oral hygiene and regular follow-up, a dental implant can last many years, even several decades.

qaList.q: Are there direct flights from Paris, Milan, Brussels or London?
qaList.a: Yes. Direct flights or short stopover flights are regularly available from several major European cities to airports serving the Sousse region.

qaList.q: What accommodations are available in Sousse?
qaList.a: Sousse offers a wide choice of accommodations: hotels, residences and apartments to suit all budgets. Our team can advise you on options close to the clinic.
